'''Josh Branson Death Star Plans''' is a [[Light]] constructed list published on Decipher Deck Designs.

== Deck info ==
* '''Player:''' [[Josh Branson]]
* '''Published:''' September 1997 (Decipher Deck Designs)
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Dagobah]]
* '''Side:''' [[Light]]
* '''Starting Card:''' {{CardLink|Dagobah: Yoda's Hut|Dagobah-L-dagobahyodashut.gif}}
* '''Strategy:''' Death Star Plans
* '''GEMP Importable deck:''' [[Media:PDag Death Star Plans Branson LS 1997.txt |Download]]

== Strategy ==

This is a deck I have used with success in tournaments. Its main weapon seems to be surprise. Players aren't quite sure how to react to its innovations, therefore affecting their decisions. Once you learn to play it correctly, it can be a great deck. It does require trading, however; some of the rares are hard to get but necessary to its proper execution. Balance it with an equally good dark deck and you can win a tournament.

== Strategy ==

Start with Yoda's Hut. Your first mission is to get Luke out so Senses become operational. With a decent hand, you should have him out at least by turn three.

One good strategy is not to use your Luke's Back as soon as you get it. Save 3 force and use it your opponent's turn. Since there is only one Luke in here, that minimizes the chance that he won't be in the deck. Then activate and deploy him, searching for Anakin's Saber and deploying. Deploy proficiency if you have it.

Your second mission is to get R2(or R5), Lift Tube, and the 3 locations. Draw until you get these, and then stop. After you have those, deploy Revolution on the Hut to set up a drain of 3 (or 4 if you have Proficiency). Deploy Lift Tube to the db 327. Deploy R2 to the y4 db.

Deploy Death Star Plans (hereafter, DSP) on the shaft corridor. Then docking bay transit R2, embark him on the lift tube, and move to the corridor. The next turn you then go back and complete DSP. I usually get 9-14, although I have gotten 18 before. Be sure only to use DSP when you have at least a 9 card lost pile (you want to maximize its effect).

If your opponent tries to deploy a lone character to a db to drain, deploy Obi-Wan and make him regret it. You can also use Surprise Assault a few times first to make him lose force. All this time, you are draining on Dagobah (hope he deploys Presence of the Force, then use I Have a Bad Feeling About This to move it to the hut to drain for 5) and using Controls on his drains.

The beautiful part is, that even though you only have 7, it seems like you have 30 after retrieving them over and over with DSP. I usually will win from between 25-35 with this deck. Traffic Control is in here to increase destiny and to guard against Monnok (although Sense can do the job).

The most ANNNOYING CARD for this deck is: "Shut him up or Shut Him Down". This card makes me mad. That is why I added Levitation. Just use this handy 6 destiny interrupt and cancel it. You could also Sense it, but that is not for sure, because of the number of fives and sixes in this deck. Monnok can also hurt, but when it is played, just pray that you win the Sense war and can draw successfully. I usually can, but you never know.

All in all, you should be able to win with this deck. Although it may look silly, it really does work. Just ask the guys who have played against it. :-)
